title: To-Do List Manager
story: Buy groceries. Finish report. Call dentist. Walk the dog. Life is a stream of tasks. A to-do list captures them, tracks completion, and gives the satisfaction of crossing things off. Build the productivity tool that runs your day.
why: A to-do list manager combines Vec for task storage, enums for status, CRUD operations (add/remove/update/list), and completion tracking — a mini database in code.
analogy: A sticky note on your monitor with tasks listed one below another. As you complete each, you draw a satisfying line through it. Your to-do list manager is the digital sticky note: add tasks to the bottom, mark them complete (strikethrough), remove done items, and always see what's left.
try_it: Add priority sorting (high priority tasks first). Add due dates and show overdue tasks. Implement a 'clear completed' function. Add task categories/tags. Save completion statistics: tasks completed today, this week, total.
tips: Use auto-incrementing IDs — each new task gets a unique identifier
In-place update: find the task by index, replace with updated version
Track completion count separately for quick stats without scanning
common_mistakes: Removing by index during iteration — indices shift, causing skipped items
Using the same ID for multiple tasks — IDs must be unique
Not handling 'task not found' — return Bool or Option for lookup results
